description: Generative answers and agentic browsers read the same site, differently. Google's own position is that this is still SEO rather than a separate discipline, so these gates are the ones where an AI reader's needs diverge from a crawler's - and nothing here trades away search to get them.

gates.title: The Site Takes A Position On AI Crawlers
gates.rule: robots.txt names the AI crawlers and allows or disallows them deliberately. Silence is not neutrality: it hands the decision to each company. Blocking Google-Extended does not affect Search, and blocking GPTBot does not stop ChatGPT citing the site through browsing.
gates.fix: Add a User-agent block per crawler with the stance the project actually wants.

gates.title: llms.txt Gives The Site's Shape
gates.rule: An llms.txt lists what the site is and where its substantial pages are. Google does not use it, so this is not a ranking gate - it is a one-fetch map for the readers that do.
gates.fix: Write llms.txt at the site root: a title, a one-line summary, and linked sections for the pages worth reading.
